gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the three picks cool by two different mechanisms (ESR and Belkin blow air with a fan; Anker pumps heat out through a thermoelectric cooler and exhausts it with a fan), that Apple's own trigger for cutting wireless charging is the iPhone's interior temperature with a 35 °C ambient ceiling, or that Anker's quiet Sleep Mode, in Anker's own words, turns the cooling off.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's ESR CryoBoost 3-in-1 25W review (cited), Macworld's best-MagSafe roundup (cited), Macworld's UGREEN MagFlow Pro 3-in-1 review, iThinkDiff's 3-in-1 roundup, and the Digital Camera World Anker Prime review (cited; body would not load, headline only). Macworld's two reviews already say heat is the bottleneck, that the iPhone throttles 25 W to 15 W or stops until it cools, and that the ESR and UGREEN fans can be switched off for bedside use, so the throttling half of the mechanism is not new. None of the pages I could read quotes Apple's actual thresholds (interior temperature, 0-35 °C ambient, the 80 percent limit when the battery is warm), none explains fan versus thermoelectric cooling, none puts the makers' cooling figures side by side, and none states that Anker's Sleep Mode turns cooling off. techgearden.com (cited) failed with a certificate error and was not read.
decides: It confirms ESR for a desk and sharpens the Anker caveat. All three cool only while the cooling is running: Anker's Sleep Mode turns cooling off, and Macworld says the ESR fan has an off button, so for overnight bedside charging in quiet mode the $229.99 Anker's thermoelectric cooler gives no cooling advantage over the $109.99 ESR. The Anker's case is daytime use in Ice Mode (charging while the phone is in use), where it is the only one of the three that names a thermoelectric cooler and claims the lowest phone temperature (below 89 °F, against ESR's below 93.9 °F as reported by Macworld). Belkin's ChillBoost is a fan like ESR's, with a maker claim of up to 12 °F cooler; the makers' figures are each from their own internal tests and are not directly comparable. Apple's wording also means no dock can guarantee 25 W: the phone itself slows or stops charging on interior temperature and may hold at 80 percent when the battery is warm.
